name: Kasba Ganapati Temple
significance: The shrine of Pune's gramadevata, traditionally traced to Jijabai Bhosale's arrival in the city around 1630. It ranks as the first of the Manacha Ganpati and was central to Bal Gangadhar Tilak's 1893 reshaping of the Ganesh festival into a public celebration.
story: The image is said to have been self-manifested and no bigger than a grain of rice at first, growing to its present size under successive coats of red sandalwood paste.

name: Kartikesvara Siva Temple
significance: A small thirteenth-century Shiva shrine standing about a hundred metres from the eastern gateway of the Lingaraja temple in Bhubaneswar's old town. It survives as a modest example of late Kalingan temple building, though vegetation and water seepage have left it in poor repair.

name: Parvati Temple, Khajuraho
significance: A small Chandela-era shrine dedicated to Parvati in the western group at Khajuraho, with a heavily restored sanctum. It forms part of the Khajuraho Group of Monuments inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Chitragupta Temple, Kanchipuram
significance: One of very few Indian temples where Chitragupta, the record-keeper who assists Yama, is the presiding deity; the masonry structure dates to the ninth century under the Medieval Cholas. It is a notable Kanchipuram landmark and holds particular importance for the Kayastha community.
story: The temple's legends explain Chitragupta's origin variously, including an account in which Shiva drew his image into being and another in which the divine cow Kamadhenu bore him as a child of Indra.

name: Kunjal Mata Temple
significance: A goddess shrine at Deh in Nagaur district set on some thirty-eight bighas of land beside the Nagaur–Ladnun road. Kunjal Mata is venerated as the kuldevi of Pareek Brahmin families of several gotras.

name: Mahavinayak Temple
deity: Mahavinayak — Shiva, Vishnu, Durga, Surya and Ganesha worshipped as one
significance: A hilltop shrine at Chandikhole whose single sanctum holds five deities — Shiva, Vishnu, Durga, Surya and Ganesha — worshipped together as one. Among the oldest Ganesha sites in Odisha, it draws pilgrims from across the state.
story: The temple is said to mark the spot where Rati's devotion won Kamadeva's release from Shiva's curse, five divine hands reaching out together for her offering to reveal the five gods present as one.

name: Lokanatha Siva Temple
significance: An eleventh-century Shiva temple in Bhubaneswar often read as a miniature prototype of the Lingaraja, and so as a trial run for that far larger project. Buried up to its bandhana and known locally as the Amuha deula, or doorless temple, it was excavated by Debala Mitra in 1972.

name: Mandodari Temple, Betki
significance: The shrine of Mandodari, a water goddess worshipped as the gramadevata of Betki village near Marcel in Goa and distinct from the Ramayana figure of the same name. Its present institution marked its centenary in 2013, though the shrine itself is held to be considerably older.
story: Villagers recount miracles worked by the water goddess and the sacrifice the village made on her account.

name: Narasimha Temple, Bhubaneswar
significance: A late-medieval shrine in Bhubaneswar enshrining a four-armed seated Narasimha, dated on architectural grounds to the fourteenth or fifteenth century. It stands within a precinct shared with other Hindu temples and is kept in good repair by the local community.

name: Nilkantheswar Shiva Temple
significance: A tenth-century Shiva temple on the western embankment of the Bindusagar tank in Bhubaneswar, locally attributed to the Kesari or Somavamshi rulers. Its niches carry parsva devata images of Ganesha, Kartikeya and Parvati, and it remains in worship at Sankranti and Shivaratri.

name: Mandhradevi Kalubai Temple
significance: A hilltop shrine about 20 km from Wai, standing at roughly 4,650 feet and held to be over four centuries old though no firm construction date is recorded. Its ten-day Kalubai Jatra each January draws more than 300,000 pilgrims, and the site became widely known after a fatal stampede there in 2005.
story: Local tradition holds that the goddess defeated demons at this hill, an event still marked by the sacrificial offerings of the annual jatra, and devotees credit the grove around the shrine with miraculous properties.

name: Mahakala-Mahakali Temple
deity: Shiva as Mahakala, with Mahakali (two lingams)
significance: An eleventh-century shrine just beyond the eastern compound wall of the Lingaraja temple, its two lingams set in yonipithas about four metres below present ground level. The superstructure is gone, leaving the sanctum itself as the surviving fabric.
story: Local tradition holds the two lingams to be the parents of Lord Lingaraja.

name: Pabaneswara Temple
significance: A grey sandstone rekha deula of the tenth century, formerly known as the Daitesvara Shiva temple, enshrining a lingam in a circular yonipitha. Heavily renovated and now hemmed in by houses and a market on three sides, little else of its history is recorded.

name: Mahamaya Dham
significance: A Shakta shrine at Bogribari in Kokrajhar district, once the tutelary deity of the zamindars of Parvatjowar and carrying a four-century-old tradition of animal sacrifice. It is regarded as Lower Assam's foremost pilgrimage site after Kamakhya.
story: The adjoining Mahamaya Snaanghat is said to be the spot where the goddess used to bathe.

name: Kumaran Kundram
significance: A hilltop Murugan shrine at Chromepet in Chennai, reached by a climb of about eighty steps and consecrated in 1979 after a proposal by the Kanchi seer Chandrashekarendra Saraswati in 1956. Modelled on Swamimalai, it draws thousands each month for circumambulation and hosts an annual Soorasamharam.
story: Devotees recount that Murugan's vel was found on the hillside as it was being cleared, which spurred the community to press on with building the temple.

name: Mallikarjuna Temple, Canacona
significance: One of Goa's oldest surviving temples, raised in the mid-sixteenth century at Sristhal in Canacona by forebears of the local Kshatriya Samaj and refurbished in 1778. Its halls, rich in wood and silver carving, house some sixty deities, and it is known for the Rajbag beach jatra and the Shisharani ritual.
story: The shrine's name is explained both by Shiva's reunion with Parvati at this spot after their separation and by his killing of the demon Malla in defence of Arjuna.

name: Paradaresvara Siva Temple
significance: A thirteenth-century Shiva shrine in the Gosagaresvara precinct off Ratha road in Bhubaneswar, built as a pancharatha with a square vimana. Only the circular yonipitha survives in the cella, and water damage has left the fabric in need of conservation.

name: Gurdwara Jand Sahib
significance: A historic gurdwara in a village some 25 km west of Faridkot city, whose history is held to be connected with Guru Gobind Singh. An old jand tree at the site is preserved along with the shrine.

name: Gurdwara Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib, Dhamtan Sahib
significance: A gurdwara at Dhamtan Sahib in Haryana's Jind district commemorating the ninth Sikh Guru, Tegh Bahadur. It is a principal Sikh place of worship for the surrounding region.

name: Gurdwara Gyan Godri Sahib
significance: A gurdwara at Har Ki Pauri in Haridwar marking a site associated with Guru Nanak's visit, built between 1866 and 1935. It was demolished in 1979 when the administration acquired the land to widen the ghat, and the site remains contested ground for the Sikh community.
story: Tradition holds that Guru Nanak, visiting Haridwar around 1504, threw water westward while Brahmins offered it to the east, telling them he was watering his fields at Kartarpur.

name: Sarvatresvara Siva Temple
place: Mahavir Lane, off Lewis Road, Bhubaneswar
significance: A Shiva temple on the road from Lewis Road toward Sisupalgarh in Bhubaneswar, dated on architectural grounds to the tenth century. It doubles as a neighbourhood gathering place for rituals, weddings and community events.
story: Local tradition credits the temple's founding to the Chedi king Kharavela, who ruled Kalinga in the first century BCE.

name: Gurdwara Guru Singh Sabha, Kedli Kalan
significance: One of the oldest gurdwaras in eastern India, completed in the eighteenth century at Kedli Kalan in Jharkhand and holding a hand-written copy of the Guru Granth Sahib some two centuries old. The congregation grew from Agrahari Sikh families who settled here from eastern Uttar Pradesh for the timber trade.
story: The site is remembered as a stop on Guru Nanak's first udasi through Bihar, where he taught the local people, and as a place later visited by Guru Tegh Bahadur travelling between Varanasi, Gaya and Patna.

name: Gurdwara Sri Guru Singh Sabha, Greater Kailash
significance: A gurdwara founded on public land by the local community in the early 1960s in Greater Kailash I, New Delhi. Alongside worship it runs the Mata Gujri Medical Centre, combining religious and welfare functions for the neighbourhood.

name: Guru Ram Rai Darbar Sahib
builtDisplay: 1699–1706 (founded mid-17th c. by Baba Ram Rai)
significance: The seat of the Ramraiya order in Dehradun, founded by Baba Ram Rai, eldest son of Guru Har Rai, on lands and funds granted by Aurangzeb; the central complex was finished in 1699 and structural work by 1706. Its minarets, domes and Mughal-style gardens and wall paintings, some over three hundred years old, are being restored by the Archaeological Survey of India.
story: The city's name is traced to the dera Baba Ram Rai pitched in the doon valley after his banishment, itself said to follow his rendering of a verse before Aurangzeb in altered words to avoid giving offence.

name: Gurdwara Guru Nanak Punjabi Sabha, Chakala
significance: A gurdwara at Chakala in Andheri East, Mumbai, built in 1956–57 and founded by Shamsher Singh Jolly to serve the local Punjabi community. The trust also runs a charitable medical dispensary and the Guru Nanak Mission High School.

name: Sanisvara Siva Temple
significance: A late-medieval Shiva shrine in the Gosagaresvara precinct at Bhubaneswar, dated to the fourteenth or fifteenth century under the Eastern Gangas. It remains in active use for Shivaratri and Durga Puja and as a venue for weddings and thread ceremonies.
story: Local tradition holds that Shiva, having unwittingly killed a calf, bathed in the Gosagaresvara tank to wash away the sin — a rite devotees still perform to expiate the killing of cattle.

name: Chirakkal Mahadeva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Puliyanam near Angamaly in Ernakulam district, counted among the 108 Shiva shrines and built in the Kerala idiom. Maha Shivaratri is its principal annual observance.

name: Rameshvara Temple, Koodli
significance: A twelfth-century Hoysala shrine at Koodli in Shivamogga district, built in an early and deliberately unornamented Vesara manner. It is protected as a Monument of National Importance, and the surrounding village — a substantial town into the fourteenth century — holds the ruins of more than eight temples and mathas.

name: Pundareekapuram Temple
deity: Vishnu, seated on Garuda with Bhudevi
significance: A Vishnu temple at Midayikunnam in Kottayam district whose sanctum shows the deity astride Garuda with Bhudevi, set within a tiled, saddle-roofed chuttambalam. It is valued chiefly for its murals, among the notable surviving examples of Kerala temple painting.

name: Patit Pavan Mandir
significance: A temple at Ratnagiri built between 1929 and 1931, conceived by V. D. Savarkar and funded and constructed by the philanthropist Bhagoji Baloji Keer with the Ratnagiri Hindu Sabha. It was founded as a temple open to all Hindus regardless of caste, and its attribution became the subject of a textbook controversy in 2025.

name: Govindaraja Perumal Temple, Chidambaram
builtDisplay: 12th–13th c.; deity reinstated by Krishnappa Nayak (1564–72)
significance: A Divya Desam to Vishnu that shares its precinct with the Nataraja temple at Chidambaram — one of only two of the 108 Divya Desams housed inside a Shiva temple complex. Largely of the twelfth and thirteenth centuries with later additions, the shrine was reinstated by Krishnappa Nayak in the 1560s and is sung in the Naalayira Divya Prabandham.
story: The site is linked to the contest in which Shiva and Parvati sought to settle which of them was the better dancer, Shiva prevailing at Tillai with the urdhvatandava pose.

name: Kumarakottam Temple
builtDisplay: rebuilt 1915; chakra vimana of the Chola period
significance: A Murugan temple standing between the Kamakshi Amman and Ekambareswarar temples at Kanchipuram, rebuilt in 1915 and retaining a Chola-period circular chakra vimana. It is one of the city's twenty-one major temples; Arunagirinathar sang its icon, and the priest Kacchiyappar is said to have composed the Kandha Puranam here.
story: The Kandha Puranam relates that Murugan imprisoned Brahma for failing to explain the syllable Om, then did penance before a linga once Shiva ordered the creator's release.

name: Mukkolakkal Bhagawathi Temple
significance: A Shakta shrine at Sreevaraham in Thiruvananthapuram whose swayambhu image is the object of a wide following in southern Kerala. Navaratri and the Ooruttu Mahotsavam in March–April are its principal festivals.
story: The shrine is said to have begun when a child at play struck a rock that then bled, and diviners pronounced the stone divine.

name: Chausath Yogini Temple, Khajuraho
deity: Devi (central cell probably Durga) with sixty-four yoginis
significance: The oldest surviving temple at Khajuraho, an open-air yogini shrine of about 885 CE with sixty-four small cells around a larger one. Uniquely rectangular among yogini temples, it attests to tantric goddess worship in the Chandela capital and forms part of the UNESCO-listed Khajuraho group.

name: Patalesvara Siva Temple – II
significance: A rekha deula of the tenth or eleventh century on Talabazar road between the Kedara-Gouri and Lingaraja temples in Bhubaneswar. Partly buried and broken, it collects rainwater so that the deity stays submerged for much of the year.

name: Ramaswamy Temple, Kumbakonam
builtDisplay: begun under Achuthappa Nayak, completed under Raghunatha Nayak (1600–34)
significance: A Rama temple at Kumbakonam begun under the Thanjavur Nayaks in the later sixteenth century and completed by Raghunatha Nayak, with later Maratha additions. Its mandapa pillars carry a pictorial Ramayana counted among the fullest renderings of the epic in Indian sculpture, and it is one of five Kumbakonam temples tied to the twelve-yearly Mahamaham festival.
story: The temple's images are said to have been recovered from a temple tank in the nearby village of Darasuram.

name: Poovattoor Bhagavathy Temple
significance: A goddess temple in Poovattoor village in Kerala's Kollam district, built in the traditional Kerala manner. It stands at about fifty metres above sea level and serves as the village's principal shrine.

name: Narayani Temple
significance: An early Odishan shrine to Durga as Narayani, dated in the sources to the seventh century and built in the Kalinga manner. The goddess is invoked here as a giver of wealth and abundance.

name: Purvesvara Siva Temple
significance: A living Shiva temple at Kancha Sahi in Bhubaneswar's old town, with vimana and jagamohana built in the mature phase of Odishan temple architecture. Its name marks it as the eastern member of a directional set around the Lingaraja, and it is looked after by a local development association.

name: Sankarananda Matha
significance: An Advaita monastery in Bhubaneswar affiliated to the Puri establishment, whose compound holds three pidha-order shrines raised over the burial places of its mahantas. The buildings are badly decayed, with vegetation growth and partial collapse.

name: Shenbagavalli Amman Temple, Payanam
significance: A goddess temple at Payanam near Marthandam in Kanyakumari district, its sanctum carried on seventeen pillars and its image shown holding a trident and a child. Its annual festival falls in late February or early March and includes a procession through the surrounding villages.
